solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Move around behind large stove

parts.note: the behind or rear is the back part
a range is a large cooking stove with several hobs and ovens

explanation.surface: Someone shifting a heavy old kitchen stove out from the back of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange furniture is to move it about into new positions, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Get to mislead, with Republican replacing Democrat

indicators.note: replacing tells us one party's letter swaps out for the other's in the word for mislead

parts.note: to mislead is to deceive
D is the usual abbreviation for a US Democrat
R is the usual abbreviation for a US Republican

explanation.surface: A cynical remark about American politics: one party's deceit simply replaced by the other's.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive something is to get it, as in getting or receiving a letter.

clue.text: Publicising longest UK road with circular shape

parts.note: the A1, Britain's longest numbered road, running London to Edinburgh, written with I for the figure one
a ring is a circular shape

explanation.surface: Promoting Britain's longest road by pointing out a roundabout on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the longest numbered road in the UK; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Airing views or grievances means making them public, so it is a synonym for publicising.

clue.text: Less common instalment of Frasier, a rerun

indicators.note: an instalment is a part of a series, so only a section of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A rare episode of the sitcom Frasier turning up as a repeat on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instalment of' takes a run of letters: the last R of Frasier, then A, then RER from rerun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarer is the comparative of rare, meaning seen less often, so it means less common.

clue.text: Encouraging sign from sleepy land?

definitions.meaning: a ... of the head signals approval or encouragement
the Land of ... is the proverbial land of sleep

explanation.surface: Someone half asleep giving a reassuring dip of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip of the head gives assent, and the Land of Nod is a jocular name for sleep.

clue.text: European, extremely old, stopping to become less hard occasionally

parts.note: very means extremely

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to soften is to become less hard

explanation.surface: An elderly European whose stiffness is easing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like it modifies 'old' but is a synonym on its own; 'stopping' puts O inside SOFTEN after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something every so often means doing it now and then, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Old-fashioned fool interrupts gym class

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym class
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A clown disrupting a school gym lesson with dated antics.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé is borrowed from French and means out of date, no longer in fashion.

clue.text: One might be attached to a parcel, a tiny bit of land?

definitions.text: One might be attached to a parcel
definitions.meaning: an adhesive paid label stuck on a parcel to send it by post
a very small garden or plot is jokingly called this, being the size of a postal label

explanation.surface: A parcel of land, in the property sense, that is laughably small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parcel' suggests the land sense as well as the postal one, blurring the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The small sticker paying for postage is one sense; the same phrase describes a minute garden or lawn.

clue.text: Flashy gem that gets waved around when guy's on fire?

definitions.meaning: slang for a diamond or other glittering jewel

definitions.text: that gets waved around when guy's on fire
definitions.meaning: a hand-held firework waved about on Bonfire Night, when effigies of Guy Fawkes are burnt

explanation.surface: A showy jewel brandished at a party where someone named Guy is doing brilliantly.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, 5 November (Bonfire Night) sees a 'guy', an effigy of Guy Fawkes, burnt on a bonfire while children wave hand-held fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: A glittering diamond is called this in slang, and so is the hand-held firework that throws out sparks.

clue.text: Bullet casing with raised line found behind barrow?

indicators.note: found behind means this piece comes after the other one

parts.note: a barrow is a small cart
a ridge is a raised line or strip

explanation.surface: A spent shell case discovered behind a wheelbarrow, perhaps at a crime scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is the case holding a bullet and its propellant charge.

clue.text: Son to possess smooth face?

parts.note: to have is to possess

explanation.surface: A wish that one's son might have a smooth-skinned face.
explanation.definitionFit: To shave is to remove stubble with a razor, leaving the cheeks smooth.

clue.text: Nice try in developing urban problem area?

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Praise for an attempt at regenerating a run-down neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The central district of a city, often associated with poverty and social deprivation.

clue.text: Name I yet find strange

indicators.note: strange signals the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled that they still find a name odd.
explanation.definitionFit: To name a suspect or species is to pick it out and say who or what it is.

clue.text: Kitchen for craft right out of art venue

indicators.note: out of tells us one letter is taken away from the art venue's word

parts.note: a gallery is where art is shown

explanation.surface: A craft fair cafe set up just to the side of an art exhibition space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like handicraft but means a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship or aircraft the cooking area is called by this name.

clue.text: Look, lad's not finished garden feature

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: not finished means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Telling someone to look at a boy's half-built garden structure.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-sided summer house set in a garden for enjoying the view.

clue.text: Gold and stone, before going without luxuries

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
st is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight of 14 pounds
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Gold and gemstones described as things one must give up when living frugally.
explanation.definitionFit: An austere life is plain and severe, doing without comforts or indulgences.

clue.text: Eye part which damage could make tear in?

indicators.note: damage suggests these letters are broken up and remade into another order

explanation.surface: A warning that harm to the back of the eye could cause a rip in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eyeball.

clue.text: Off-the-shoulder end of Teeswater held by wire fastener beside ship

indicators.note: held by means the letter sits inside the fastener's word

parts.note: a staple is a bent wire fastener

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of Teeswater

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A sheep fleece, Teeswater being a breed, pinned with wire beside a boat, oddly described as a dress style.
explanation.walkthrough: Teeswater is a British breed of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapless dress leaves the shoulders bare, which is what off-the-shoulder describes.

clue.text: Someone acting for another in favour of two unknowns

parts.note: pro means in favour of
x and y are the standard unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A deputy who supports two unidentified people.
explanation.definitionFit: A proxy is a person authorised to vote or act on another's behalf.

clue.text: Fool accepting second surprising plot development

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish character who agrees to be a second, a classic story turn.
explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected turn in a story's plot, as in a twist ending.

clue.text: Goddess of beauty atrophied terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: The goddess of beauty has wasted away dreadfully.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of love and beauty, the counterpart of Roman Venus.

clue.text: Layer often found in batteries?

parts.note: an egg-laying bird kept in rows of battery cages, not a layer of chemicals in an electric cell

explanation.surface: A question about the layered construction inside electrical batteries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' reads as a stratum and 'batteries' as electrical cells; in fact they mean an egg-producing bird and factory-farm cages.
explanation.definitionFit: Battery farming keeps laying birds in small cages, so the egg producer is found there.

clue.text: Beam of light in contact with synthetic fabric

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
on means touching, in contact with

explanation.surface: Light shining onto a man-made cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a man-made textile fibre made from cellulose.

clue.text: Aircraft circling fringes of eastern New York, which Beatles sang about

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the plane's word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

indicators.note: fringes are the edges, so the first and last letters of eastern are taken

explanation.surface: An aircraft circling over New York, with a nod to the Beatles' song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which Beatles sang about' is an unusual definition: it names a famous Liverpool street by its song rather than by meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liverpool street immortalised in the 1967 Beatles song of the same name.
